steps.name: fire_notification_reminder_24h_capturing
steps.result: BLOCKED — pre-empted by the LIVE production notifications_worker, then confirmed harness bug on isolated retest
detail: The seeded appointment fell inside the live reminder_24h window (23-25h) and was picked up for REAL by the always-running `atrevete-notifications` container within ~30s of seeding — BEFORE the capturing fire_notifications.py could be invoked. This is a genuine production-safety gap: any QA scenario that seeds a PENDING/CONFIRMED appointment inside a notification window on this shared DB races the live worker, which does NOT use the capturing client.

docker logs atrevete-notifications (19:48:09-19:48:11 UTC) show a REAL send attempt: resolved ConversationHistory.conversation_id='900051', attempted send into Chatwoot conversation 900051 (does not exist), got rejected, then created_conversation_with_template FOR REAL — creating a real Chatwoot contact (contact_id=42639) and a real Chatwoot conversation (conversation_id=126) for the sandbox phone +34999000051. appointments.reminder_sent_at was stamped 2026-07-05T19:48:11Z, well before my own fire_notifications.py invocation at 19:48:30Z.
Running fire_notifications.py --handlers reminder_24h afterward correctly found 0 eligible rows (reminder_sent_at already set) — send_attempts: 0.

Isolated unit-level retest (constructing fire_notifications.py's _make_capturing_handler + a fake Appointment/ConversationHistory, no live DB/Chatwoot touched) reproduces a hard failure: `AttributeError: '_CapturingClient' object has no attribute 'send_template_to_conversation_checked'`. tests/e2e/harness/fire_notifications.py's _CapturingClient mocks the OLD ChatwootClient API (`send_template_message` / `create_conversation_with_template` returning bool), but agent/workers/notification_handlers/_delivery.py.deliver_template() (the current context-coherence D1-D6 code) calls `chatwoot.send_template_to_conversation_checked(...)` returning a `ConversationSendOutcome` enum for the RESOLVED-conversation branch. The capturing harness was never updated for this refactor, so it will ALWAYS crash on exactly the scenario it's meant to validate (an appointment whose customer has a resolvable canonical ConversationHistory row) — the only branch that doesn't crash is the resolver-miss/fallback branch (which only exercises create_conversation_with_template, still mocked correctly).

Net effect: the notification-threading assertion (send_attempts[0].conversation_id == '900051' && fallback_conversation_created absent) could NOT be safely/correctly captured via the documented procedure. It is BLOCKED by a stale test harness, independent of whether the application's disclosure fix is correct.

bugs_found.summary: tests/e2e/harness/state_reset.py has no CLI entrypoint; SKILL.md Steps 2/8 document running it directly as a script, which silently no-ops. The real reset logic (Redis + DB) is only reachable via `qa_turn_helper.py reset`.
bugs_found.impact: Every QA run that followed SKILL.md literally for Steps 2/8 has been skipping sandbox hygiene and cleanup entirely, with no error surfaced. This likely affects prior batches, not just this run.
bugs_found.fix_suggestion: Either add a __main__/argparse block to state_reset.py, or correct SKILL.md Steps 2 and 8 to reference `qa_turn_helper.py reset` instead.

bugs_found.summary: tests/e2e/harness/fire_notifications.py's _CapturingClient mocks the pre-context-coherence ChatwootClient API (send_template_message/create_conversation_with_template -> bool) but agent/workers/notification_handlers/_delivery.py.deliver_template() now calls chatwoot.send_template_to_conversation_checked(...) -> ConversationSendOutcome for the resolved-conversation branch.
bugs_found.impact: The capturing harness crashes with AttributeError on exactly the scenario this test (and D1/D2 of context-coherence) is meant to validate — a customer with an existing resolvable ConversationHistory row. It only survives the resolver-miss/fallback branch. This scenario's step-4 assertion cannot currently be exercised safely.
bugs_found.fix_suggestion: Add `send_template_to_conversation_checked` to fire_notifications.py's _CapturingClient, returning ConversationSendOutcome.SENT (recording conversation_id) analogous to the existing send_template_message mock.

bugs_found.summary: The always-on production atrevete-notifications worker polls the shared DB continuously and will process any QA-seeded PENDING/CONFIRMED appointment that falls inside a real notification window (23-25h for reminder_24h, etc.) before a QA harness capturing run can intercept it, sending real WhatsApp/Chatwoot API calls for fabricated sandbox customers.
bugs_found.impact: This run caused a real Chatwoot contact + conversation to be created for a fake +34999 number in production.
bugs_found.fix_suggestion: For scenarios needing an appointment inside a live notification window, either seed with reminder_sent_at/confirmation_sent_at already stamped (to make the row ineligible for the live worker) and unset it in the same transaction as the harness call, or pause the notifications worker during this specific scenario, or (preferred, more robust) fix bug harness-bug-fire-notifications-stale-capturing-client and additionally gate the live worker's query by a phone-prefix exclusion in non-prod-safe test windows.
